title: Memorandum On S.M.C. Economy

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, WEDNESDAY, NOVEMBER 11, 1931
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
& S. C. REGISTRY
No. S. B. D. 2885.
11. 11. 31.

S.M.Police

MEMORANDUM ON S.M.C.
ECONOMY

Shanghai Chinese Ratepayers Association
on Reducing Expenses

ON the subject of Municipal Economy the "North-China Daily News" has been supplied, through the courtesy of the Shanghai Chinese Ratepayers Association, with a copy of the letter which that organization has addressed to the Shanghai Municipal Council.
The writers of the letter suggest:
(1) The disbandment of the Municipal Orchestra or its transfer to private operation:
(2) The appointment of capable Chinese to senior positions in the Council's service:
(3) The extension of road widening programmes, etc., over a larger number of years so that the rate of progress will not prove burdensome on the Budget of any particular year
(4) That reduction of pay should commence with the higher paid officials.
The full text of the letter follows:—

Bankers Building,
4, Hongkong Road, S'hai.
November 9, 1931.
The Chairman,
Shanghai Municipal Council,
Shanghai.
Sir,—We beg to bring to your attention and the attention of the Council the following Memorandum on the subject of Municipal Economy:

MEMORANDUM
Governments, national, provincial and municipal, in levying taxes for their support and for meeting their multifarious obligations must have definite policies in financial administration. The financial policy of the pre-War countries was in the main directed toward the adjustment of the countries' incomes to their expenditures, or in other words the various governments were concerned in taking out as much from the pockets of their people as was needed by the public treasuries in financing their huge budgets entailed principally by military expansion. After the War, however, the countries have turned to the direction of adjusting their expenditures to their incomes or in other words they have endeavored to take out from the pockets of their people only what is within their ability to give. This brings us to the criterion of taxation: the government should build up a public income by withdrawing from private incomes only those amounts roughly calculated on the basis of the people's ability to pay. The public need of money and the people's economic capacity should therefore be maintained in a state of equilibrium. If such equilibrium is at times disturbed, the public should be contented to curtail its expenditure rather than endeavoring to increase its revenue by imposing additional burdens upon the taxpayers.

Lessen of the War
The Great War has left in its wake unprecedented financial stringency to the vanquished nations but it does not follow that the victors are in any way well off. Indeed, during the decade after the War, we find practically the whole world groaning under economic difficulty which has culminated in the recent trade depression yet unabated. The effects of this crisis upon the administrative policies of the various nations so far perceptible are the retrenchment movement in Japan, the war debt moratorium proposal of President Hoover and the formation of a coalition government in Great Britain following the collapse of the Labour Cabinet on the budget question. The formation of a country's policy, therefore, has to follow the general trend of economic development of the country and the world.
Now in turn to Shanghai, unquestionably the greatest financial centre of China and the meeting place of the traders of all cities and countries. Local market in Shanghai, however, depends for its prosperity mainly upon the business conditions in the Yangtze provinces and south and north China, and it has for the past months felt severe setback as a consequence of the flood visitation and the Japanese Manchurian invasion which have brought business in both central and north China practically to a standstill. The Shanghai residents while contributing large funds to the rescue of the flood refugees have at the same time been deprived of business profits, and their conditions are by no means as happy as they were before. The fact that a large number of native houses and shops are at present left vacant in the International Settlement and the French Concession and comparative...

Q. & I. Please reply and forward to Registry & F.R.O.
Please file.
12/11/31.

I. P. T. O.

《字林西报》，1931年11月11日，星期三
上海公共租界工部局警务处
及 S. C. 登记处
编号：S. B. D. 2885。
1931年11月11日。

上海公共租界警务处

关于工部局
节约开支的备忘录

上海华人纳税会
关于削减开支事宜

就市政节约这一主题，《字林西报》承蒙上海华人纳税会惠赐该组织致上海工部局信函副本一份，现予刊登。
去函者建议：
(1) 解散工部局乐队，或将其转由私人经营；
(2) 任命能干的华人担任工部局服务部门的高级职位；
(3) 将道路拓宽等计划延长至更多年份实施，以免进度过快而对任何特定年度的预算造成沉重负担；
(4) 减薪应从高薪官员开始。
信函全文如下：—

上海，香港路4号，
银行大楼，
1931年11月9日。
致：
上海工部局主席，
上海。
先生，— 谨提请阁下及工部局注意以下关于市政节约事宜的备忘录：

备忘录

国家、省及市政府在征收税款以维持自身运转并履行其繁杂义务时，必须在财务管理上拥有明确的政策。战前各国的财政政策主要致力于调整国家收入以适应其支出，换言之，各国政府关注的是从民众口袋中取出公共金库为 principally 由军事扩张引起的庞大预算融资所需的金额。然而，战后各国已转向调整支出以适应收入的方向，或者说，它们努力只从民众口袋中取出其能力范围内所能给予的部分。这就引出了征税的标准：政府应仅基于民众支付能力粗略计算出的数额，从私人收入中提取部分以建立公共收入。因此，公共资金需求与民众经济能力应保持平衡状态。如果这种平衡有时受到干扰，公众应满足于削减开支，而不是试图通过向纳税人施加额外负担来增加收入。

战争的教训

大战给战败国留下了前所未有的财政紧缩局面，但这并不意味着战胜国就境况良好。事实上，在战后的十年间，我们发现几乎整个世界都在经济困难中呻吟，这最终导致了近期仍未缓解的贸易萧条。迄今为止，这场危机对各国行政政策的影响显而易见，包括日本的紧缩运动、胡佛总统提出的战争债务延期偿付提案，以及英国工党内阁因预算问题垮台后联合政府的成立。因此，一个国家政策的制定必须顺应该国及世界经济发展的总体趋势。
现在轮到上海，毫无疑问，上海是中国最大的金融中心，也是各城市和国家商人的汇聚之地。然而，上海本地市场的繁荣主要取决于长江流域各省以及中国南北地区的商业状况，而在过去的几个月里，由于水灾侵袭和日本入侵满洲，上海市场遭受了严重挫折，这使得华中和华北的商业几乎陷入停滞。上海居民在为救助水灾难民捐献巨额资金的同时，也失去了商业利润，他们的处境远不如从前那样安乐。目前，在国际租界和法租界内，大量本国房屋和店铺空置，相比之下……

问 & 我。请回复并转发至登记处及外侨登记处（F.R.O.）。
请归档。
1931年11月12日。

I. P. T. O.

Retrenchment Wanted
Under such circumstances, it will certainly meet with public approval that the financial policy to be pursued by the Council should be one of retrenchment and economy and should not be directed toward the exploration of the source of revenue, in order to maintain balance in the Municipal Budget. This Association in consideration of the economic capacity of the Rate-payers beg to urge the Council to embark upon an extensive economy scheme in its administration with particular reference to the reduction of administrative expenses and the discontinuance of non-essential services.
There are two ways in which to appropriate money for municipal purposes, namely positive and negative. The former relates to those items in the municipal budget which will yield productive returns to the public treasury, such as capital expenditure on public utilities, while the latter relates to such items as educational appropriation which do not give immediate and tangible returns in terms of dollar or cent. In this latter group, a saving in the number of the municipal ledger may mean irreparable loss to the community and eventually to the government. There is however, still a third and this we refer to the expenditures on police, public health, etc., which should be so fixed as to be commensurate with the services performed. For instance, increase of criminal cases will necessitate the enhancement of police strength and hence the police expenditure, and this enhancement is justified only by a decrease in crime returns. It is certainly not in the interests of economy to have a race between the increase of police expenditure and the growth of criminal cases. Economy in this third group, therefore, is measured by the degree of efficiency with which any particular duty is performed.

The Four Suggestions
In the following, we beg to suggest four practical ways which will have applicable effects in the direction of economizing municipal administration and alleviating the burden in the Council's Budget, which the Treasurer and Controller has informed us will be in the neighbourhood of Tls. 2,000,000 for the year 1932.
(1) The Municipal Orchestra, which is now an established institution has absorbed the Council's revenues of approximately Tls. 100,000 per annum should be disbanded or at least considerably reduced in size and cost. The present orchestra is composed of about forty musicians, many of whom are highly paid Europeans. We feel that the time has come when the Council should consider whether such an expensive luxury can be justified in these days of economic depression. We suggest that the orchestra be reduced to a minimum or entirely abolished, and the funds thus saved be applied to more essential services.

The Police Force
(2) The expenditure for Police Force at present constitutes about 39 per cent. of the total Municipal revenue, but if the senior officers could be replaced by competent Chinese, the expenses in the form of salaries, allowances and bonuses can be curtailed to an appreciable extent. The same is true not only of the Police Force but of all other Municipal Departments. This Association is consistent in its proposal of employment of capable Chinese in the senior positions of the Council's service for various considerations of which municipal economy is undoubtedly an outstanding one. In this connection, it may be mentioned that a material saving will accrue to the Council under the item of exchange compensation if the Municipal service can be open to more local Chinese appointments.
(3) The capital expenditure on road extensions and widenings bears heavily on the Municipal Budget, and steps should be taken in mapping out a measure of relief to the Council's finance in this direction. While this Association fully appreciates the relations between road improvements and municipal development and the effects road projects will have of enhancing the value of the adjoining lands and the revenue of the Council, it is equally aware that increased land assessments will bring about a corresponding increase in house rentals and will materially affect the cost of living of the bulk of the population. Since road projects are undertaken in the interests not only of the present Ratepayers but of the future, they should be so planned as to enable the programme to be extended to a period of years and consummated only by progressive stages. The projects should not be executed with such degree of velocity as will prove burdensome to the Budget of any particular year.

A Delicate Suggestion
(4) We have noted that the Council is considering whether the personnel of certain Departments can be maintained at the present level, but wish to point out that the salaries paid to some incumbents of senior positions are higher than appear to be either necessary or equitable as compared with those paid to the rank and file of the staff. The wage at present paid to a constable is not sufficient to enable him to have a settled life under the existing living conditions while the remuneration received by some senior officers may be too high. We fully appreciate the gravity of this aspect of the question, but do suggest that retrenchment in this direction of curtailment of personnel expenses should start with the upper end of the Council's staff list. It is reported in the papers that Mr. Ramsay MacDonald voluntarily relinquished one thousand pounds of his annual salary as an aid to the retrenchment policy of the British Government. This may be a lesson to all of us.
We beg to bring to the Council's consideration the above four suggestions and to record as concluding remarks our opinions that municipal economy should be effected only in so far as it does not affect the expenditures which are vested as capitals in productive undertakings or are intended for educational purposes, that efforts should be made to ensure maximum return by entailing minimum cost in the conduct of technical services, and that exploration of the source of revenue in the direction of increased taxation should be avoided as far as possible. We beg to request that the Council extend to our proposals its careful consideration in the interest of the welfare of the community in the Settlement.
Yours faithfully,
SHANGHAI CHINESE RATE-PAYERS ASSOCIATION

亟需紧缩

在这种情况下，工部局所采取的财政政策若是紧缩和节约，而非着眼于开拓财源，以维持市政预算的平衡，肯定会得到公众的认可。本会考虑到纳税人的经济承受能力，谨敦促工部局在行政管理中实施广泛的节约计划，特别侧重于减少行政开支和取消非必要的服务。
为市政目的拨款有两种方式，即积极方式和消极方式。前者涉及市政预算中能为公共金库带来生产性回报的项目，如公用事业的资本支出；而后者涉及教育拨款等不能以元或角分的形式立即产生有形回报的项目。在后一类中，市政账目数量的节省可能意味着对社区乃至最终对政府造成无法弥补的损失。然而，还有第三类，我们指的是警察、公共卫生等方面的支出，这些支出应根据所提供的服务量来确定。例如，刑事案件的增加将 necessitate 增强警力，从而增加警察开支，而这种增加只有在犯罪率下降的情况下才是合理的。让警察开支的增长与刑事案件的增长之间进行竞赛，显然不符合节约的原则。因此，第三类的节约程度是以执行任何特定职责的效率来衡量的。

四项建议

下文谨提出四种切实可行的方法，这些方法将在节约市政行政管理和减轻工部局预算负担方面产生适用效果，据财务长兼主计长告知，1932年的预算赤字约为白银200万两。
(1) 工部局乐队现已成为一个既定机构，每年消耗工部局约白银10万两的收入，应予解散，或至少大幅缩减其规模和成本。目前的乐队由约四十名乐手组成，其中许多人是高薪聘请的欧籍人士。我们认为，在经济萧条时期，工部局应考虑这种昂贵的奢侈是否合理。我们建议将乐队缩减至最低限度或完全废除，并将由此节省的资金用于更基本的服务。

警队

(2) 目前警队的支出约占工部局总收入的39%，但如果由能干的华人接替高级警官，薪金、津贴和奖金形式的开支可大幅削减。这不仅适用于警队，也适用于所有其他工部局部门。本会一贯提议在工部局服务部门的高级职位上雇用能干的华人，出于各种考虑，市政节约无疑是其中突出的一项。在这方面，值得一提的是，如果工部局服务部门向更多本地华人开放任职，工部局将在汇兑补偿项目下获得实质性的节省。
(3) 道路延伸和拓宽的资本支出给市政预算带来了沉重负担，应采取步骤规划措施，以此方向缓解工部局的财政压力。虽然本会充分理解道路改善与市政发展之间的关系，以及道路项目对提升周边土地价值和工部局收入的影响，但同样意识到，土地估值的增加将带来房租的相应上涨，并将严重影响大多数人口的生活成本。鉴于道路工程不仅是为了现任纳税人的利益，也是为了未来的利益，其规划应使计划能够延长至数年，并分阶段逐步完成。工程的执行速度不应快到对任何特定年度的预算造成负担。

一项微妙的建议

(4) 我们注意到，工部局正在考虑是否可以将某些部门的人员维持在现有水平，但希望指出，一些高级职位在职人员的薪金高于看似必要或公平的水平，与普通职员相比更是如此。目前巡捕获得的工资不足以使其在现有生活条件下过上安定的生活，而一些高级官员获得的薪酬可能过高。我们充分认识到这个问题方面的严重性，但确实建议，在削减人员开支方面的紧缩应从工部局职员名单的上层开始。据报道，拉姆齐·麦克唐纳先生自愿放弃其年薪中的一千英镑，以协助英国政府的紧缩政策。这对我们所有人来说或许是一个教训。
谨提请工部局考虑上述四项建议，并在结束语中记录我们的观点，即市政节约应在不影响作为生产性企业资本投入或用于教育目的的支出的范围内实施，应努力确保在开展技术服务时以最低成本获得最大回报，并应尽可能避免通过增加税收来开拓财源。谨请求工部局为了租界社区的福祉，仔细考虑我们的提议。
此致，
敬礼，
上海华人纳税会

III J
